title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this part of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', 𝔊 is a finite quotient of the profinite modular group SL(2,ℤ)^ (or its image modulo ±1). ρ and σ are the images of the elliptic generators ρ = (0 1; −1 1), of order 6 (order 3 mod ±1), and σ = (0 −1; 1 0), of order 4 (order 2 mod ±1). G_{ρ,σ} is an ambient group containing 𝔊. Z_ρ and Z_σ are centralizers in G_{ρ,σ}, and δ_ρ, δ_σ are homomorphisms to a small abelian group γ_{ρ,σ} (= Γ_{ρ,σ}). That group has two distinguished subgroups γ' and γ''. Plausibly γ_{ρ,σ} is a group of 'exponent' data (ℤ/3)^* × (ℤ/4)^* ≅ {±1}², recording whether an element sends the generator to itself or to its inverse; this reading is inferred, not stated on the page.

The previous page proves the following. Im δ_ρ contains γ', and equals all of γ iff ρ ~ ρ^{-1} in 𝔊; likewise Im δ_σ contains γ'', and equals γ iff σ ~ σ^{-1} = −σ in 𝔊. There, SL(2,ℤ/3)' is used to show Im δ_ρ = γ'. The conjugators of ρ to ρ^{-1} in GL(2,ℤ/3) are f τ'_∞ with f = cρ + d. The determinant condition becomes c² + cd + d² = −1 mod 3, which is impossible.

This page has two parts.

(1) Easy case. If σ² = 1 (i.e. we are in a quotient where −1 = 1), then σ = σ^{-1}. Hence Z_σ → γ_{ρ,σ} is surjective.

(2) Main claim, the 2-adic analogue. Suppose 𝔊 has SL(2,ℤ/4) as a quotient, emphatically 'sans ′', i.e. not modulo ±1, since in PSL(2,ℤ/4) one has σ = σ^{-1}. Then Im δ_σ = γ''. The proof shows σ and σ^{-1} are not conjugate in SL(2,ℤ/4):
- τ_∞ = diag(−1,1) conjugates σ to σ^{-1}.
- σ is regular (cyclic) mod 2, so its centralizer in M_2(ℤ/4) is ℤ/4[σ].
- Hence all conjugators in GL(2,ℤ/4) are g = f τ_∞ with f = tσ + u.
- det τ_∞ = −1, so det g = 1 forces det f = t² + u² = −1 ≡ 3 mod 4.
- This is impossible, since squares mod 4 are 0 and 1.

The obstruction is local in an instructive way. For odd p, −1 is always a sum of two squares mod p. So σ ~ σ^{-1} in every SL(2,𝔽_p) with p odd, and only level 4 detects the non-rationality of the class of σ. Similarly, the norm form of ℤ[ω] is surjective mod p for p ≠ 3, so only level 3 detects ρ ≁ ρ^{-1}.

(3) Crossed-out start of a construction. Kernels are defined:
- SZ_ρ = Ker δ_ρ = Z_ρ ∩ 𝔊 = Centr_𝔊(ρ);
- SZ_σ = Ker δ_σ = Centr_𝔊(σ);
- SB_{ρ,σ} = Ker δ_B = B_{ρ,σ} ∩ 𝔊 = L_0.
A fibre-product subgroup is also sketched: S_0M_{ρ,σ} ⊂ B × Z_ρ × Z_σ × C, cut out by δ_B(u) = δ_𝔊(U) = δ_σ(b) = ε_3(μ) δ_ρ(a). This is abandoned. The next page instead introduces τ_B = (τ, −1), the semidirect extension 𝔊' = {1,τ}·𝔊, and the normalizer N_σ = {1,τ_B}·Z_σ of ⟨σ⟩.

Purpose. The aim is to control the 'sign' parts of the centralizers of the elliptic elements. In modern terms, this asks whether the conjugacy classes of the order-3 and order-4 generators are real/rational. That governs the action of complex conjugation (λ = −1 in the cyclotomic/GT action σ ↦ σ^λ) on branch-point inertia for modular-type dessins.
errors: No mathematical error. The proof leaves implicit the fact that the centralizer of σ in M_2(ℤ/4) is ℤ/4[σ] (true because σ is cyclic mod 2). This fact justifies the claim that all conjugators have the form (tσ+u)τ_∞.
The step 'det(g)=1 signifie det f = −1 i.e. t²+u² = −1, impossible' is written in scrambled order on the page, but the logic is correct.
Strictly, one only needs the image of σ in 𝔊 to be non-conjugate to its inverse. This follows because conjugacy in 𝔊 would descend to the quotient SL(2,ℤ/4); the argument is valid as stated.

ideas.what: σ = (0 −1; 1 0) is not conjugate to σ^{-1} in SL(2,ℤ/4), via the determinant of conjugators fτ_∞ with f ∈ ℤ/4[σ] and the fact that t²+u² ≠ −1 mod 4.
ideas.modern_name: Non-real (non-rational) conjugacy class of the order-4 elliptic element; level-4 obstruction via sums of two squares
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (classical computation of conjugacy classes in SL(2,ℤ/n))

ideas.what: Criterion: the image of the 'sign' map from the centralizer of an elliptic generator is everything iff the generator is conjugate to its inverse; trivially surjective when σ² = 1 (PSL case).
ideas.modern_name: Real conjugacy classes and centralizer/normalizer index-2 extensions (N(⟨σ⟩)/C(σ) ⊂ Aut⟨σ⟩)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; used in rationality/rigidity criteria (Belyi, Thompson, Matzat)

ideas.what: Fibre-product subgroup S_0M_{ρ,σ} of B × Z_ρ × Z_σ × C defined by compatibility of the δ maps (crossed out).
ideas.modern_name: Fibre product of stabilizers over a group of 'cyclotomic' exponent data

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary and correct verification (σ ≁ σ^{-1} in SL(2,ℤ/4) via sums of two squares mod 4), parallel to the ℤ/3 computation on the previous page. It is well known and routine; the surrounding construction is only set up, then crossed out.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Si P[?] contenu[?] 𝔊 contient[?] comme[?] quotient[?]' should read 'Si par contre 𝔊 contient comme quotient SL(2,ℤ/4ℤ)'; the crossed-out 'ℤ/4ℤ' precedes it.
'(sans[?] !!)' is '(sans ′ !!)', i.e. SL(2,ℤ/4ℤ) without the prime (not modulo ±1), contrasting with SL(2,ℤ/3ℤ)' on the previous page.
The target group is written with lowercase gamma (γ_{ρ,σ}, γ''_{ρ,σ}), consistent with the previous page, rather than Γ.
